questions: Did this weakness develop gradually over weeks or months, rather than coming on suddenly?
Does the weakness get noticeably worse with activity and improve with rest?
Do your eyelids droop, especially toward the end of the day or when you are tired?
Do you have difficulty swallowing or chewing?
Have you noticed any slurring of your speech?
Do you have any numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation in your arms or legs?
Have you had any infection, such as a cold, flu, or gastroenteritis, in the past month?
Does anyone in your family have a similar muscle or neurological condition?
Do you have any back or neck pain?
Do you have any trouble with bladder or bowel control?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1 (hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy type 1)

Alternatives:
1. Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) - particularly given the sudden awareness of weakness
2. Guillain-Barré syndrome superimposed on an underlying hereditary neuropathy
3. Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies (HNPP)
